meta.tagline: Reconstruct a web app from what your browser already received
meta.intro: Your browser downloads every line of a web app's code and every byte of its data. raider records that, redacts the secrets, and rebuilds the app as a project that installs and runs.

stages.title: Three stages, one seam
stages.lede: The browser is the only place the app is alive. Everything that needs a running page happens in the extension; everything else happens offline, where iteration is cheap. They meet at a documented bundle on disk.

capture.name: Capture
capture.body: The extension attaches the DevTools protocol to your tab and records every request and response — JavaScript, HTML, JSON, assets — plus the framework, router table, and chunk manifest it can only read while the page is running.

bundle.name: Bundle
bundle.body: One zip. Deduplicated bodies addressed by hash, a redacted request log, discovered source maps, and an explicit list of everything the capture missed.

reconstruct.name: Reconstruct
reconstruct.body: The CLI recovers original sources, infers a typed API from observed payloads, and emits a project with a replay server. The skill hands the rest to Claude Code or Codex.

extension.title: The capture extension
extension.lede: Chrome's extension API cannot read response bodies. The DevTools protocol can — so raider attaches it directly, which is why Chrome shows the "being debugged" banner while you browse.
extension.cdpBody: Request and response bodies, WebSocket frames, and the sourceMappingURL of every script — even when the comment was stripped from the served file.
extension.coverageBody: It reads the bundler's own chunk manifest and the live router table, then shows you what you haven't loaded yet. You navigate; the meter drives you to complete coverage.
extension.redactionBody: Credentials never reach disk. A token becomes a stable placeholder — the same token gets the same placeholder everywhere, so the auth flow stays reconstructable without a single real credential leaving the browser.
extension.installBody: Not on the Web Store. Build it and load it unpacked.

bundle.title: What's in a bundle
bundle.lede: Open it with unzip and read it with jq. Nothing about the format is proprietary.
bundle.gapsBody: A reconstruction built over silently missing chunks produces confident, wrong output. Anything the capture failed to record lands in gaps.json, propagates into the generated code as an RAIDER-GAP marker, and makes the replay server answer 501 instead of inventing a response.

cli.title: The CLI
cli.lede: Every deterministic stage runs here: source-map recovery, JSON Schema inference across observed payloads, endpoint clustering, and code generation.
cli.outputBody: A project that installs, typechecks, and builds — plus the intermediate artifacts every stage wrote, so you can re-run any stage without capturing again.

skill.title: The skill
skill.lede: The CLI does what is mechanical. The skill carries the judgment: read the artifacts, implement one route at a time against the endpoints that actually fired, and never invent what the capture did not see.
skill.codexBody: Codex reads ~/.codex/skills. It also honours ~/.agents/skills, the alias Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI share, so one install can serve several agents.
skill.installBody: One command per runtime. It symlinks the skill, so it tracks the repository — and it is safe to re-run.

walkthrough.title: Reversing an app, start to finish
walkthrough.lede: The whole loop, in the order you'd actually do it.
walkthrough.s1: Open the app and start capture. Chrome shows the debugging banner — that's the protocol attaching.
walkthrough.s2: Navigate everywhere. Watch the coverage meter: every lazy chunk that hasn't loaded and every route you haven't visited is a hole in the reconstruction.
walkthrough.s3: Review what was redacted, then export. You get one zip.
walkthrough.s4: Run the CLI. It recovers original sources when the app shipped maps, and infers types from real payloads when it didn't.
walkthrough.s5: Point your agent at the output. It reads the report first, then implements route by route.

repos.title: Four repositories
repos.lede: The library is imported by the extension, so it holds no filesystem or Node APIs. The CLI needs both, which is why it lives apart. This site is the fourth.
repos.extension: MV3 capture: DevTools protocol, offscreen buffer, coverage meter, redaction, export.
repos.cli: Reconstruction CLI and the agent skill. Unzip, analyze, generate, replay.
repos.lib: Bundle format, redaction, coverage, schema inference. No I/O, by construction.
repos.web: This landing page. React, Vite, Tailwind, deployed on Cloudflare Pages.

footer.note: raider reads what a browser was already given. That's ordinary practice for interop work, security research, and rebuilding your own applications. Pointing it at someone else's property is a decision you own — their terms, and your jurisdiction, both have opinions.
footer.built: Built with Bun, Vite, and the Chrome DevTools Protocol.
